extracted.intended_audience: Predoctoral fellowship applicants (F99/K00), mentors, and grant administrators preparing or responding to NIH F99/K00 reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Review criteria and reviewer guidance for NIH F99/K00 Transition to Aging Research for Predoctoral Students fellowship applications, covering evaluation of the applicant, mentors/collaborators, training plan, institutional support, human subjects protections, inclusion, RCR training, budget, and scoring procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact: reviewers' summary judgment of the application’s potential to have a sustained, powerful influence on the research field and the applicant’s development into an independent scientist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative summaries synthesizing strengths and weaknesses determine the Overall Impact. Reviewers note integration and coherence of the F99 and K00 phases, mentoring quality, institutional support, and whether training and research are likely to lead to an independent research career. The review explains that applications judged by the SRG as not in the top meritorious group are unlikely to be funded. (Footnote: impact/priority score is calculated by averaging voting reviewers' overall scores (1-9) and multiplying by 10.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the applicant’s potential for a productive scientific career, current productivity, scholarly record, relevant experience, and preparedness for proposed training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate strengths such as relevant research interests, prior research assistantships, academic performance, awards, and demonstrated motivation; evaluate weaknesses such as limited publication record (many items 'in preparation' vs. published), ambiguous productivity, or insufficient prior training for technically demanding methods. Consider whether the applicant's planned activities (e.g., grant writing, coursework, clinical exposure) are appropriate for career development and whether time allocations (e.g., teaching/mentoring vs. training) are balanced for this mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsors, Collaborators, and Consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the quality, relevance, and adequacy of mentors and collaborators to provide the proposed training and research mentorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths include a diverse multidisciplinary mentoring team with relevant expertise and productivity. Weaknesses include missing essential clinical or methodological expertise (e.g., geriatric psychiatrists, neurologists, neuropsychologists, neuroimaging experts, biostatisticians specializing in imaging). Reviewers may recommend adding mentors with specific clinical or technical skills and increasing frequency or modes of interaction with distant mentors. Assess whether mentors’ commitments and roles are clearly justified and sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Training Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the proposed training and research plan for clarity, coherence, rigor, and suitability to the applicant's career development goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the training plan is systematic and detailed (timing, frequency, activities), includes appropriate didactic and practical experiences, and aligns with the research aims. Look for a clear conceptual model and appropriate methodologies. Weaknesses include overly broad or underdeveloped pieces (e.g., many disparate components without integration), insufficient clinical experience, lack of formal quantitative coursework for complex methods (e.g., imaging statistics), unrealistic expectations about self-learning (e.g., equating R programming with mastery of statistics), insufficient time allotted for grant writing, and lack of consideration of challenges in planned studies (e.g., trial attrition, protocol deviations). Justify added components (e.g., rationale for qualitative focus groups within a quantitative program).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the likelihood that the proposed training will develop the applicant into an independent, productive investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths include applicant motivation and reasonable mixture of new training; weaknesses include incomplete development of mentorship or training elements that reduce enthusiasm. Evaluate whether the proposed experiences and mentorship will provide necessary skills for independence, including opportunities for publications, advanced methods training, and grant-writing experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Environment & Commitment to Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the institutional setting, resources, facilities, and institutional commitment are adequate to support the proposed predoctoral and postdoctoral training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths include access to strong resources at named institutions, committed K00 site/institutional mentors, and appropriate facilities. Weaknesses include lack of clear commitment to provide specific resources tailored to the fellowship (even if the general environment is excellent). Consider whether multi-institutional arrangements may affect frequency of contact with distant mentors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether risks to human subjects are acceptable and protections are adequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers note 'Acceptable Risks and Adequate Protections' when all major elements are addressed and there are no SRG concerns. Check that human subjects involvement is certified and that protections are described; flag any unresolved risks or inadequate protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate plans for inclusion of diverse participant groups by sex/gender, race/ethnicity, and age, and justification for any exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application should justify distributions scientifically: Sex/Gender, Race/Ethnicity, and Inclusion/Exclusion Based on Age. Age exclusions should be justified when the study legitimately focuses on a particular age group (e.g., older adults). Reviewers expect explicit justification of inclusion/exclusion criteria and adequate plans to ensure representative participation where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the adequacy of proposed RCR training in format, subject matter, faculty participation, duration, and frequency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark 'Acceptable' when RCR plans address all major elements. The document lists that Format, Subject Matter, Faculty Participation, Duration, and Frequency should each be described and are expected to be addressed for all initiatives. Reviewers look for multiple initiatives (e.g., four different initiatives) with these elements clearly described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the requested budget and period of support are appropriate for the proposed training and research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may state 'Recommend as Requested' when budget and period appear appropriate. Assess whether resources requested are justified, realistic, and sufficient to support the training plan and research activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring and Review Process / Administrative Scoring Notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rules governing how criterion scores and overall impact scores are submitted and calculated during peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion scores are submitted by assigned reviewers prior to the SRG meeting and are not discussed specifically at the meeting nor are they calculated into the overall impact score at the meeting. The overall impact (priority) score is calculated by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers and multiplying by 10. Some applications also receive a percentile ranking. Applicants are referred to NIH peer review process documentation for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human/Animal Subjects Involvement (administrative status)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative indication of whether human or animal subjects are involved and their certification status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the sample: 'Human Subjects: 30-Human subjects involved - Certified, no SRG concerns' and 'Animal Subjects: 10-No live vertebrate animals involved for competing appl.' Ensure correct classification and certification; unresolved or misclassified subjects can raise SRG concerns.
